# CS2 IP Changer

> Free Windows app (Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit) for Counter-Strike 2 that routes CS2 and Steam through an Android phone's mobile data, so community servers see the carrier's IP and not the player's home IP. It keeps the home IP out of community server logs and ban lists without a VPN (servers see an ordinary mobile connection, so it also works where VPNs are blocked), and after an IP ban on a community server the player changes IP from the app and joins again. It is not a VPN and does not touch the game process, its memory or its files.

Website: https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/
Source and downloads: https://github.com/Sepd0x/cs2-ip-changer (latest release: https://github.com/Sepd0x/cs2-ip-changer/releases/latest)
Download: https://github.com/Sepd0x/cs2-ip-changer/releases/latest/download/CS2IPChanger.exe (CS2IPChanger.exe, 63.4 MB, SHA-256 441e9ae0c8def2de90c83cfdec3c531a963a8370d5418a5ae0c7f43887bd6517, VirusTotal: 0 of 69 engines flag it, https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/441e9ae0c8def2de90c83cfdec3c531a963a8370d5418a5ae0c7f43887bd6517/detection)
Status: beta. Latest release 0.1.0-beta.9 (2026-11-03). Free, no account. Not affiliated with Valve.

## How it works

- The phone shares its mobile data with the PC over USB tethering or its Wi-Fi hotspot. A 4G/5G USB dongle or router also works as the connection.
- The app adds Windows routes so CS2, Steam and the servers on the user's list go through the phone, and blocks them on the home connection. The browser, Discord and downloads stay on the home connection (Game only mode). The whole PC can go through the phone instead.
- Kill switch (shown in the app's Checks as "Block if the phone drops"): a Windows Firewall rule blocks the listed servers on every adapter except the phone, and cs2.exe's game traffic (UDP) can only use the phone connection. If the cable comes out, the game loses connection instead of falling back to the home IP. Until a phone has been connected once, CS2 is not locked, and in No phone mode nothing is blocked.
- Change IP: turns mobile data (or airplane mode) off and on over ADB until the carrier gives a new IP. It can report whether the new IP is in a new /16 range and keep trying until it is.
- Needs admin rights (routes and firewall rules are system settings), Windows Firewall on, and an Android phone with mobile data. USB debugging is needed only to change IP from the PC.

## Features

- Change IP and rejoin after a kick or an IP ban, also from inside the game with a hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+F10 by default). After a ban it also logs into the next Steam account that server hasn't banned.
- Live checks of Windows Firewall, routes, the IP servers see next to the home IP, whether the phone is really on mobile data and whether Steam uses the same connection as the game, plus a leak test.
- Connection quality: ping, jitter and loss through the phone every 30 seconds.
- Server list from IP:port or steam://connect links with name, map, players and ping; can wait for a slot on a full server.
- Steam account switcher for alt accounts: uses the logins Steam already saved, switching never asks for passwords (only the optional Profiles sign-in does, and it keeps an encrypted sign-in token, never the password); shows VAC, game and trade bans and cooldowns; marks server bans per account and community. New IP + next account (Ctrl+Shift+F9) gets a new IP, logs into the next account in rotation and rejoins the last server.
- CS2 config manager: copies binds, crosshair, game settings, video and HUD/radar/audio between accounts, with backups, snapshots and compare.
- Profiles: changes the Steam name, picture, bio, country, privacy and custom URL of chosen accounts from templates, with preview and restore.
- Regions: picks where CS2 matchmaking can put the player, with ping per region; turned-off regions are blocked by one Windows Firewall rule for cs2.exe on Valve's relay IPs only.
- Phone setup: steps for the cable, USB driver, USB debugging, tethering and the phone's Wi-Fi that check themselves (green or red), with a button where the app can do the step.
- Protection starts off each time the app opens; Turn on protection (Status or the tray icon) turns it on until you turn it off.
- No phone mode: play on the home connection (not protected) while accounts, configs, profiles and regions keep working.

## What it is not

- Not a VPN or proxy: servers see an ordinary mobile connection from the player's carrier, so it also works on community servers that block VPN and datacenter IPs.
- Not a cheat and no VAC bypass: it does not hide cheats from any anti-cheat. A ban on a Steam account follows the account; a new IP does not lift it.
- Will ping be worse? Usually, yes: mobile data adds latency and jitter compared with a home connection.
- Who sees the IP: on community servers joined directly, the server admins and their plugins. Official matchmaking goes through Valve's relays (Steam Datagram Relay).

- [Steam profile editor](https://sepd0x.github.io/cs2-ip-changer/steam-profile-editor/): name, avatar and privacy on many accounts.

## Safety and privacy

- Releases are built by GitHub Actions from the public source, with a build attestation and a SHA-256 file.
- Updates install only if the SHA-256 matches and is signed with the project's offline key, which is not on GitHub.
- The exe is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns the first time.
- Usage stats in the beta, required to use the app: the first start shows what is sent, with Accept and Quit (Quit closes the app without changing anything). Once when the app has been open for 20 seconds, when it closes, and once a day, with a random ID made for this install, with no name, never from the PC or the user (Delete my stats in Settings deletes it all): versions, country, mode, how the phone is connected, minutes open, button counts, a few counters, list sizes and errors. Nothing is sent and no ID is made before Accept. Never IPs, servers, accounts or names; the server stores no IP.
- Save bug report saves a .zip on the Desktop and sends nothing. It leaves out the current and last home IP, API key, logins, names, SteamIDs, e-mails, Wi-Fi names and the Windows user.
- Third parties: ipwho.is receives the home IP and the phone's IP when the app shows their carrier and city (each asked only through its own connection); ipify, icanhazip, Amazon and Cloudflare see the IP they measure; Steam, Google (ADB download) and GitHub (updates) get normal requests.
- It never opens CS2's memory and never injects into the game: it changes Windows routes and firewall rules, and which Steam account logs in.
